name: Team Dresch
label: Chainsaw
lede: Two zine-and-label operations, one hurdling Mariel Hemingway on the T-shirt, and a queercore band that booked its first tour over AOL.

eras.title: A zine, a label, a phone tree
eras.text: Before there was a band, there was Donna Dresch's zine Chainsaw and a queercore scene stitched together by mail. Dresch, Jody Bleyle and Kaia Wilson found each other through it, and booked a first tour on AOL message boards.

years.h: Donna Dresch plays bass for [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]] on tour
years.p: Dresch filled in on bass for [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]]'s 1990 US and Australian tour, years before anyone heard her own band.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the Dinosaur Jr. stint alongside a stretch as a temporary replacement in [[Screaming Trees|bc5e6e42-73ba-44fa-a41e-3379402f0429]]. It was a working musician's résumé built next to a zine: Chainsaw, which ran alongside her contributions to Outpunk, Homocore and Tobi Vail's Jigsaw.

years.src: Wikipedia: Team Dresch · Vortex: Team Dresch Remember Who They Are · OPB: Pioneering Northwest punk band
years.h: Team Dresch forms: Donna Dresch, Jody Bleyle, Kaia Wilson, Marcéo Martinez
years.p: Wikipedia dates the band to Olympia in 1993; Vortex Magazine says Portland in 1994. Either way the four-piece was a queercore band from its first show.
years.xp:
Vortex reports that Wilson wrote to Dresch after reading Chainsaw. Bleyle was already drumming in Hazel and running Candy Ass Records; Dresch had started Chainsaw Records in the early 1990s. Vortex mentions their T-shirt art of Mariel Hemingway hurdling, from the film Personal Best.

OPB adds that the group booked its first tour in 1993 using AOL message boards and email, which makes a van full of queer punks an early adopter of the internet.

eras.title: Personal Best
eras.text: A Kill Rock Stars single, a festival slot in Olympia and a debut LP made in five days. Chainsaw and Candy Ass, two labels run by two members of the band, put it out themselves.

years.h: "Hand Grenade" 7-inch lands on Kill Rock Stars
years.p: The band's first record is a single on Kill Rock Stars, with "Endtime Relay" and "Molasses in January" on the other side.

years.h: Five days at Avast! in Seattle with John Goodmanson
years.p: The band cuts the ten songs of Personal Best in five days with producer John Goodmanson, then goes home and starts mailing it out.
years.xp: Wikipedia's page on the album gives August 1994 and Avast! studio in Seattle. The finished record runs about 24 minutes.

years.src: Wikipedia: Personal Best · Wikipedia: Team Dresch
years.h: Personal Best: 24 minutes, two labels, zero closet
years.p: Wikipedia dates the release to January 23, 1995, on Chainsaw and Candy Ass, and lists "Hate the Christian Right!" and "Freewheel" among its ten tracks.
years.xp:
AllMusic's Jason Ankeny wrote that it "explodes on contact." The Washington Post called it "a fiery, all-but-forgotten punk masterpiece." Wikipedia says it had sold more than 20,000 copies by 2004, and Rolling Stone placed it at number 48 on a 2026 list of greatest punk albums.

The title nods to the 1982 lesbian-themed film of the same name.

years.h: Jody Bleyle's Candy Ass releases the double LP Free to Fight
years.p: The compilation of all-women bands comes with a 75-page booklet of self-defense advice, and the band carries the idea out on the road.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia's Candy Ass page the label's other artists included [[Sleater-Kinney|e36e78eb-3ace-4acd-882c-16789e700ab7]], [[Excuse 17|bad37a2a-1ab8-4605-b8f3-e0615cd7de64]], [[Heavens to Betsy|8716a313-c6df-440c-9b74-370e8d79728e]] and Hazel. Its promised singles series ended after one release, a Sleater-Kinney and Cypher in the Snow split, because of money.

eras.title: New drummer, more teeth
eras.text: Melissa York takes the drum stool, the band goes deeper into politics and self-defense, and then it comes apart. The pieces become The Butchies.

years.src: Wikipedia: Team Dresch · Wikipedia: Melissa York
years.h: Melissa York replaces Marcéo Martinez on drums
years.p: York, who had come up in New York hardcore with Born Against, joins for the second album.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Melissa York page lists Born Against, The Manacled and Vitapup among her earlier bands, and dates her Team Dresch years to 1993 onward; the band's own page puts her replacing Martinez in 1996.

years.h: Captain My Captain, the record after the breakdown
years.p: Bleyle says much of her writing came from a physical and emotional breakdown before the sessions at John and Stu's Place in Seattle.
years.xp:
The album came out on Chainsaw and Candy Ass on June 4, 1996, with Goodmanson producing again. It has eleven songs, including "Uncle Phranc" for the folk singer Phranc, who guests, and "Don't Try Suicide." It closes on "Remember Who You Are," over eight minutes long. Pitchfork later scored it 8.8 out of 10.

Wikipedia describes it as a more outwardly queer record than Personal Best, with mental health in the frame.

years.src: Wikipedia: Team Dresch · Discogs: Team Dresch / Bikini Kill
years.h: Bikini Kill and Team Dresch share a spring tour 7-inch
years.p: [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]] and Team Dresch put out a split single named for their Spring Tour 1996, one of several splits the band made that year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Team Dresch · Wikipedia: Candy Ass Records
years.h: On screen in She's Real (Worse Than Queer)
years.p: Lucy Thane's documentary on riot grrrl and queercore puts the band in front of a camera; Bleyle also talks about Candy Ass and Free to Fight in it.

years.big: Two of the four leave for North Carolina. One of them takes the drummer.
years.src: Vortex: Team Dresch Remember Who They Are · Wikipedia: The Butchies · Wikipedia: Kaia Wilson · Wikipedia: Team Dresch
years.h: Kaia Wilson and Melissa York move to North Carolina and form The Butchies
years.p: Wilson and York leave to start [[The Butchies|adf334c2-9186-48cd-afcc-c748dd47e9b4]], whose first album Are We Not Femme? arrives the same year.
years.xp:
Vortex reports the original lineup imploded after a tour, with strain in the relationship between Bleyle and Dresch. Wilson had already co-founded Mr. Lady Records with Tammy Rae Carland in 1996, and The Butchies' first three albums came out on it.

The band's last release of the first run was The New Team Dresch V 6.0 Beta, a 7-inch on Outpunk.

eras.title: Homo-a-Go-Go and the sporadic years
eras.text: The band returns for a festival and keeps coming back a few shows at a time, on its own terms.

years.h: Team Dresch headlines Homo-a-Go-Go in Olympia
years.p: Six years after splitting, the band headlines Olympia's queercore festival, and keeps playing occasional shows afterward.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists sporadic West and East Coast tours in 2006 and 2007, an appearance at Outfest in California, Pacific Northwest shows in 2009 and 2014, and two shows at Ladyfest in Brazil in May 2010. The band has described its approach since as taking things day by day.

years.h: Queercore: How to Punk a Revolution
years.p: Yony Leyser's documentary features the band alongside the scene that made them.

eras.title: Twenty-five years on
eras.text: Reissues, a Portland Pride weekend and a first new song in 19 years. The story since has been about credit and catalogue.

years.src: Vortex: Team Dresch Remember Who They Are · Wikipedia: Team Dresch
years.h: Jealous Butcher reissues the whole catalogue
years.p: Jealous Butcher Records puts out both albums and the singles collection Choices, Chances, Changes for the 25th anniversary.
years.xp: Vortex gives the reissue date as May 31, 2019, and two Portland shows at Mississippi Studios on June 14 and 15 for Pride weekend. Marcéo Martinez came out publicly as transmasculine that year, and the reissued credits were corrected; Wikipedia quotes him calling that "so important and necessary" for visibility.

q: Your music stopped me from killing myself
letter to the band, per Bandcamp Daily
years.src: Bandcamp Daily: The Power of Community · Wikipedia: Team Dresch
yt: Women of Rock Oral History Project, 2018
years.h: "Your Hands My Pockets": first new song in 19 years
years.p: A 2019 single, and a new video for "Fagetarian and Dyke" that uses previously unseen live footage.
years.xp: Wilson told Bandcamp Daily the band was pretty inactive but had decided to get more active. She also said they get letters from young people. One reads:

years.h: "Story of the Earth" goes to the Trans Justice Funding Project
years.p: Written in 2007 after colony collapse disorder made the news, the single sends all proceeds to Trans Justice Funding Project.
According to Wikipedia's Donna Dresch page, the band is inducted into the hall in 2023.
OPB reports the band on the road for the record's 30th birthday, with both Martinez and York among the drummers.
